subsystems.name: Reflector / mirror
subsystems.role: a star-sized, curved sheet that reflects the star's light so its emission is no longer symmetric.
parts: aluminium-coated polymer film a few micrometres thick

subsystems.name: Statite positioning
subsystems.role: holds the mirror in place against gravity without orbiting.

subsystems.name: Thermal and materials protection
subsystems.role: keeps the film from softening or evaporating near the star.

subsystems.name: Energy collection (Class B designs)
subsystems.role: a swarm of collectors captures the star's output to power active jets rather than only reflecting light.

subsystems.name: Mass ejector and nozzles (Class B designs)
subsystems.role: turns stellar material into directed plasma jets.
parts: energy beams focused on the stellar surface

subsystems.name: Control and repair
subsystems.role: keeps a structure a million times wider than any built object working for geological time.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap a mining and manufacturing base
buildSteps.detail: Mass launched from Earth is far too expensive, so the process would start with self-replicating robots mining asteroids or a moon for metals, silicon and carbon.

buildSteps.title: Make mirror film in space
buildSteps.detail: Aluminium is vapour-deposited onto a polymer film only a few micrometres thick. It must be made and handled in microgravity, since no gravity-well factory could make sheets this large and this thin.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the mirror at the star's pole
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of film panels and their frames rendezvous, dock and unroll into one curved reflector, positioned above one pole of the star.

buildSteps.title: Balance the mirror as a statite
buildSteps.detail: The mirror is not put in orbit. Radiation pressure from the star's own light pushes it outward while gravity pulls it inward; the two are balanced so it hangs in place.

buildSteps.title: Create asymmetric radiation
buildSteps.detail: Because the reflected light is redirected rather than escaping isotropically, the star-plus-mirror system has a net momentum imbalance. The mirror's gravitational pull on the star transmits that small thrust to the star itself.

buildSteps.title: Add active jets for a faster engine
buildSteps.detail: In 'Class B' designs — for example the Caplan thruster proposed in 2019 — a swarm of collectors gathers stellar energy, focuses it on a small spot on the star to blast material off as a directed plasma jet, and fires a second, counter-jet to keep the engine itself from being pushed into the star.

buildSteps.title: Steer and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Slow changes of mirror angle or jet direction would steer the system. Over millions of years, robotic repair and recycling would replace damaged segments.

prerequisites.why: the thrust a mirror feels from starlight is understood and measured; it is simply very weak.

prerequisites.tech: Ultra-thin reflective films and large deployable structures
prerequisites.why: solar sails and spacecraft sunshields have deployed thin reflectors tens of metres across, but not square kilometres.

prerequisites.tech: In-space manufacturing and assembly at scale
prerequisites.why: no factory has ever built structures hundreds of kilometres wide in space.
the mass needed cannot come from Earth; it has to be made from off-world material by machines that build their own replacements.
the machinery must keep working, and repairing itself, for far longer than any human institution or device has operated.

pathway.milestone: small solar sails prove that light alone produces measurable thrust
pathway.unlocks: a real, if tiny, force to build on.

pathway.milestone: kilometre-class deployable reflectors and orbital assembly
pathway.unlocks: the engineering vocabulary of very large, very light structures.
megastructure mass without launching it from Earth.

pathway.milestone: a partial Dyson swarm capturing a large fraction of a star's output
pathway.unlocks: the energy budget for active engines and for star lifting — removing material from the star for fuel.

pathway.milestone: a complete Shkadov thruster able to move a whole star system
pathway.unlocks: relocating a solar system away from a dying star, or toward another one, on a timescale of millions of years.
